slots.title: 50% U.S. tariff hits ~$20B Canada imports
slots.body:
A 50% tariff is now in place on roughly $20 billion of Canadian imports.

Talks between the U.S. and Canada broke down late Friday.

The levy took effect at 12:01 a.m., per weekend trade coverage.

That policy line landed as U.S. benchmarks had already finished higher on the prior cash session:

- $SPY proxy ^GSPC +0.4% to 7,674.37
- ^DJI +1.0% to 53,277.01

The fear gauge eased on that close:

- ^VIX -5.5% to 15.13

Which part of the Canada trade story are you tracking first — goods categories, timing, or the next negotiation headline?

slots.title: Up to 300,000 tons beef import tariff pause
slots.body:
Up to 300,000 metric tons of ground beef can enter the U.S. for 90 days with no out-of-quota tariff.

Coverage frames it as targeted relief on ground beef to ease consumer grocery costs.

The same announcement included a commitment that qualifying beef would be sold at 25% below current market prices.

That food-policy headline sits beside a softer oil complex in the cross-asset tape:

- Brent -3.6% to 90.96
- WTI proxy $USO +0.1% to 134.64

Long-dated Treasury yields from the Aug. 21 snapshot:

- 10-year 4.7%
- 2s10s spread 0.5 percentage point

Do you read this beef import carve-out mainly as a grocery-price story or as part of the wider tariff toolkit?
